questions.q: What does a Rank table calculation with the Competition (1,2,2,4) option do when two values are tied?
options: Both tied values get the same rank, and the next rank skips ahead by the number of tied rows
Both tied values get different, arbitrarily-assigned ranks
Ties are not allowed and Tableau throws an error
Tied values are automatically removed from the view
questions.explain: Competition (1,2,2,4) mirrors SQL's RANK() function: tied rows share a position, and the rank following the tie jumps ahead by the number of tied rows (skipping rank 3 in this example).

questions.q: How does Dense ranking (1,2,2,3) differ from Competition ranking (1,2,2,4)?
options: Dense ranking does not skip a position after a tie, matching SQL's DENSE_RANK(); Competition ranking does skip, matching SQL's RANK()
They are identical — just two names for the same thing
Dense ranking can only be used with numeric fields, and Competition ranking only with text fields
Dense ranking always ranks in ascending order, while Competition ranking always ranks descending
questions.explain: Dense ranking does not leave a gap after a tie (the next distinct value gets the very next integer), while Competition ranking skips ahead by the number of tied rows — the same distinction as SQL's DENSE_RANK() versus RANK().

questions.q: What does a Percentile table calculation express, as opposed to a Rank calculation?
options: Where a value falls as a percentage of the range, rather than as a whole-number position
The exact same thing as Rank, just multiplied by 100
Only whether a value is above or below the median
The count of values tied with the current one
questions.explain: Percentile expresses a value's position as a percentage — the lowest value in the partition scores 0% and the highest scores 100% — rather than assigning a whole-number rank position.

questions.q: What is Year over Year Growth, underneath the quick calculation menu?
options: A pre-configured Percent Difference From, set up to compare each year to the previous one
An entirely separate calculation engine unrelated to any other table calculation
A pre-configured Rank calculation
A calculated field, not a table calculation at all
questions.explain: Year over Year Growth is really just Percent Difference From with Compute Using and Relative To already configured to compare each year to the prior one — a shortcut, not a new mechanism.

questions.q: What is YTD Total, underneath the quick calculation menu?
options: A pre-configured Running Total that restarts at the beginning of each year
A pre-configured Percent of Total scoped to the current year
A brand-new calculation type with no relationship to Running Total
A filter that hides all data except the current year
questions.explain: YTD Total is a Running Total with Restarting Every already set to the year boundary, giving a proper year-to-date accumulator without manually configuring Restarting Every yourself.
